query: How can sellers improve Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: performance_vs_expectation
per_column.rationale: Categorizing how the product met expectations gives a strong axis to group complaints vs praise, directly supporting the 'how to improve satisfaction' query. Values are mostly sound readings (AMZ-0004 works_as_advertised, AMZ-0005 works_as_advertised, AMZ-0002 shortfall). Weaker on AMZ-0001, where the grievance is availability/lack of a product rather than a product underperforming, so 'significant_shortfall' is a loose fit, but not egregiously invented.

per_column.name: content_or_creative_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Provides a distinct axis focused on creative/content problems (narrative, factual accuracy, bias), complementing the performance dimension rather than restating it, useful for media products in the review set. Values are well grounded: AMZ-0002 political commentary weighed against faith writing maps reasonably to narrative/pacing weak; AMZ-0004 skincare correctly not_present; AMZ-0005 meets_expectations. AMZ-0003's music rant as 'narrative_or_pacing_weak' is a defensible categorization of shallow lyrical content.

judge.rationale: Both columns supply genuine, non-redundant categorical axes that let an analyst segment reviews by product performance and by content quality, directly enabling insight into what sellers could improve. Neither is near-constant nor a trivial sentiment flag. Values are largely well-grounded extractions/categorizations of the source text, with only mild stretch on rows where the grievance type doesn't cleanly fit the schema (e.g., availability complaint coerced into a performance shortfall). No clear hallucinations of invented facts observed.
